## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> One of the 4 named giants; the TOC catalogue carries a per-dataset lastUpdate change-feed, so refresh only whole dataset codes whose lastUpdate moved instead of the blind skip-if-exists crawl.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Eurostat TOC catalogue (catalogue/toc/txt) per-dataset lastUpdate/lastModified column; persist code->lastUpdate state map and re-fetch only codes whose upstream lastUpdate is newer (plus brand-new codes).
- `since_param`: n/a (no obs-level since; unit-level change-feed via TOC lastUpdate, not startPeriod — this profile is the bulk SDMX-TSV dissemination path, format=TSV&compressed=true, not the per-obs SDMX query API)
- `out_paths_note`: WRITES TO TWO DIRS/STAGES: raw data/raw/eurostat/<code>.tsv.gz (~7,640 files, fetch_eurostat_bulk.py) AND clean_full/eurostat/<CODE>.parquet (~7,753 files, separate ingest_eurostat.py). A true delta must purge/refetch only changed raw codes then reparse only those in ingest (today ingest reparses ALL; its advertised --delta flag is a no-op).
- `rate_note`: No key. Polite UA, 6 concurrent workers, 4 retries linear backoff on 429/5xx, 300s timeout, atomic .part->replace. Constraint is sheer volume (~7,600 datasets, multi-GB, ~6.1B obs); legacy files/ bulk path is 410 Gone.

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/eurostat.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/eurostat.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S4 fetcher — Eurostat (one of the four named giants, ~7,600 datasets, ~6.1B obs).

Change-feed: the dissemination catalogue TOC
  https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/catalogue/toc/txt
is a tab-separated, quoted table whose columns are
  title | code | type | last update of data | last table structure change | data start | data end | values
Rows of type `dataset`/`table` are real datasets; `folder` rows are not. The
"last update of data" cell (DD.MM.YYYY) is the per-dataset vintage: re-fetch only
codes whose lastUpdate moved (plus new codes, plus any flow whose last run was
partial/failed/empty/absent).

Per changed flow: incremental SDMX-CSV pull
  .../sdmx/2.1/data/<code>/?format=SDMX-CSV&startPeriod=<last_obs+tail>
merged into clean_full/eurostat/<CODE>.parquet (series_key, obs_date, value).

STABLE series_key — the load-bearing fix:
  The SDMX-CSV columns are DATAFLOW, `LAST UPDATE`, <dims...>, TIME_PERIOD,
  OBS_VALUE, OBS_FLAG, CONF_STATUS. The legacy ingest joined ALL non-time/value
  columns as `k=v`, so `LAST UPDATE` (a SPACE, which slipped past the LAST_UPDATE
  underscore skip-set) AND OBS_FLAG/CONF_STATUS leaked into the key:
      LAST UPDATE=13/05/26 11:00:00:freq=A:...:OBS_FLAG=e
  Because `LAST UPDATE` changes EVERY release, every series got a brand-new key on
  every publish -> the whole file duplicated. Here the key is built from the
  DIMENSION columns only (everything strictly between `LAST UPDATE` and
  TIME_PERIOD), so it is STABLE across releases. lastUpdate is carried in the
  change-feed sidecar, not the key. See the RE-KEY data-op note in
  giant_changed_units.py for the existing-data migration (designed, NOT executed).
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/fetch_eurostat_bulk.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='eurostat'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source eurostat --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source eurostat --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('eurostat');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter read as a year is silent and has hit 7 sources.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source eurostat
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
